title: Inference sprint hackpack — sales labs (annotated)
body:
Purpose:
Quick, portable pack for SEs and SDRs running small ‘inference sprint’ workshops with engineering/product partners. Focus is on a 60–90 minute hands-on lab + one-pager battlecard snippets reps can drop into customer threads. Not a full pitch deck — this is tactical, annotated speaker notes + troubleshooting cues.

Overview (what to bring to a sprint):
- 10–12 minute primer slide set (3 slides): problem framing, Redwood value props (latency/cost/reliability), pilot outcomes. Speaker note cues included below.
- 30–45 minute lab: live sample app + optional local/private deployment demo (if customer asks).
- 10–15 minute Q&A and next-step commit (pilot scope + success metrics).

Annotated slide outline (speaker cues):
1) Slide: WHY inference economics matter — one-liner + micro-case (e.g., chat support saving 35% cost per ticket). Cue: ask "what's your per-interaction cost target?"
2) Slide: Where teams leak ops $$$ — batching, cold starts, model mismatch. Cue: drop in sample token-cost graphic and ask about burst patterns.
3) Slide: Redwood tactical levers — routing tiers, prefix caching, quantization profiles, reserved capacity. Cue: call out canary fallback policy (if model A slow -> auto route to cheaper variant).

Lab runbook (minimal friction):
- Pre-flight: confirm region, API key & test app (repo link above), baseline tokens per call estimate.
- Boot: show 2 runs (hosted vs dedicated sim): latency & cost dashboard snapshot.
- Experiment: change batching window or enable prefix caching; show measured delta (latency vs unit cost).
- Wrap: capture a screenshot of Console metrics, propose a 2-week pilot (SLO: 95th latency target + cost savings target).

Battlecard snippets (copy-paste for Slack/email):
- Value starter: "Redwood reduces per-token spend by combining KV caching + model routing; we typically see 20–40% unit cost improvement in retrieval-heavy workflows."
- Objection: "We can't trust fallbacks." Response: "Canary+tracing shows fallbacks only used under capacity stress; we ship the same model family variants and can configure graceful degradation thresholds."
- Security ask: "Can deploy in VPC/HSM" -> "Yes, we have private control plane + KMS integrations; we can run a closed pilot inside your VPC."

Troubleshooting pocket (notes to SE):
- If demo app returns blank tokens: check model version pin and runtime kernel (console logs -> kernel mismatch warning).
- If latency spike at 95th: inspect batching window and cache hit rate; temporarily reduce batch window to preserve P95.
- If customer nervous about cost: show short A/B with quantized variant and auto-fallback band.

Success metrics (for pilot handoff):
- Operational: P95 latency <= customer target (ms).
- Economic: unit cost reduction (%) vs baseline.
- Safety: no P0 errors in 2-week pilot, tracing enabled.

Playbook TODOs (quick):
- [ ] Create 3 one-line customer-specific value statements for finance, legal, platform.
- [ ] Produce 1-page PDF of the demo run steps (for CSM handoff).
- [ ] Add a short checklist for SRE handoff if pilot moves to Dedicated.

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep lab to code-lite: prioritize Console snapshots and observable deltas over deep infra talk unless asked.
- Prep a fallback economics slide (example numbers) — customers respond to clear unit-cost math.
- Gather 2 micro-case outcomes from recent pilots (NDA-friendly stats).

Attachments (links): repo + small sample dataset + quick dashboard template are in the linked artifacts.

End of doc — use this as the base for lightweight SE-led pilot activations.
